<img src="resources/cmvividly_logo.png" alt="CMVividly" class="home-logo" />

I'm Damon May ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/damonhmay){target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"}), a machine learning researcher and computational immunologist.
I was most recently at Adaptive Biotechnologies, in both leadership (Associate Director)
and individual contributor (Principal Scientist, most recently) roles, building ML models on
immune receptor repertoires.

Here, I'm sharing insights about a resource my colleagues and
I made available in July 2026: The **CMV ECOcluster**. 
We mined >30,000 T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoires to find **ECOclusters**:
groups of TCRs that tend to occur in the same people. Each ECOcluster putatively represents
humanity's collective, shared response to a virus, bacterium or other prevalent exposure
([preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.03.26.583354){target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"} in bioRxiv,
[explainer](https://globalforum.diaglobal.org/issue/january-2025/#ecoclusters){target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"} in DIA Global Forum)

The **CMV ECOcluster** ([download](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.03.26.583354v3.supplementary-material){target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"})
is a sensitive, specific, quantitative
biomarker of T-cell response to Cytomegalovirus (CMV). Each of its 52,447 TCRs is associated
with the Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) allele that presents the CMV peptide it binds.
